claims.text: Optimized plasma surface treatment can significantly improve the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in extreme corrosive environments.
Combining plasma treatment with a chemical coating may further improve corrosion resistance.
The native surface of untreated stainless steel fails under extreme corrosive conditions.
A machine-learning model trained on experimental plasma-treatment and chemical-coating data can be used to optimize the surface-treatment process.
High-chloride and acidic environments degrade untreated stainless steel.
The treatment forms a uniform, passivating oxide or composite surface layer.
Plasma treatment induces controlled surface modifications that form a high-quality passive film.
A chemically coated, plasma-modified surface better resists corrosive attack.
Machine-learning-optimized process parameters enable reproducible high corrosion performance.
Treated stainless steel will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than untreated stainless steel under the same extreme conditions.
Treated stainless steel will retain greater structural integrity than untreated stainless steel under the same extreme conditions.
The expected effect is limited to the tested plasma-treatment and coating-parameter ranges and to corrosive conditions similar to those used for optimization.
